title: tiered-canary-briefing-panel-with-explainable-assertions-prototype
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers need a concise, actionable briefing when a canary/A-B experiment starts showing anomalous signals. Current rollouts UI surfaces raw metrics but lacks an at-a-glance interpretation and quick remediation controls. This ticket prototypes a compact briefing panel (Tiered Canary Briefing Panel) that appears in the rollouts header and in the timeline flyout. The panel summarizes risk, confidence, suggested actions, and exposes a small set of high-confidence controls (pause, throttle to X%, emergency rollback, rollforward) with a short explanation for each suggestion.

Goals:
- Provide engineers with a one-line risk summary and a top-3 explainable reasons for the signal (e.g., latency spike in region eu-west-1, increased 5xx on rerank route, quality regression on prompt set).
- Surface statistical confidence and duration needed to reach significance.
- Offer safe, limited remediation actions that can be taken from the briefing panel with two-step confirmations and clear audit prompts.
- Integrate with existing telemetry and rollout rules so actions respect org policies (e.g., only PMs can rollback across multiple services).

Out of scope for this ticket: deep experimentation analytics, long-form runbook editor, analytics correlation UI (separate).
acceptance_criteria: Panel shows one-line risk summary with severity badges (low/medium/high) and color-coded indication
Panel lists up to three explainable assertions that contributed to the risk score (each with drilldown link to metric/traces)
Statistical confidence widget displays current p-value/ci and estimated time-to-significance based on recent traffic pattern
Quick actions include Pause, Throttle (preset slider: 10/25/50/100), Rollforward, Emergency Rollback and each requires two-step confirmation with reason field
Actions are gated by role-aware policies (UI reflects disabled actions if user lacks permission)
Prototype flows validated with 3 engineering participants and 2 PMs in design review session, with recorded feedback in comments
Design tokens and components align with console-2025.03 theme and accessible contrast ratios
design_notes: Briefing panel appears collapsed by default; expands on hover or when alert crosses medium threshold
Explainable assertions generated by backend scoring service (placeholder copy used in prototype)
Use confidence microchart (sparkline + shaded CI) rather than large chart to keep panel compact
Throttle control is constrained by rollout policy and shows resulting QPS estimate inline
Emergency rollback disables throttle and sets traffic to 0% for variant; rollforward is a guarded action that advances primary traffic to variant if flagged as safe
Audit trail modal included in confirmation flow to capture reason, approver, and linked PR/incident if any
tasks: Finalize microcopy for assertion reasons and confirmation modals
Handoff Figma frames and interactive prototype to frontend (links in attachments)
Work with backend to map explainable-assertion payload schema (fields: reason, weight, evidence_link)
Add role-check call in frontend before enabling quick actions
Run moderated usability test with 5 engineers and 2 on-call SREs
Iterate on compact layout for 320-1440px breakpoints
decisions: Keep panel compact and optional; do not auto-open full rollout editor on every alert
Limit quick actions to 4 to reduce cognitive load (Pause, Throttle, Rollforward, Emergency Rollback)
Show confidence time-to-significance using a 95% CI by default
Require two-step confirmation for any action that changes traffic by >25% or performs rollback
If a user lacks permission, show contextual help and an "Request approval" action (opens modal to ping approvers)
